content.title: Red Sox-Reds recap: Crochet deals in Opening Day pitchers' duel
content.text: What to KnowGarrett Crochet: 6.0 IP, 3 H, 0 ER, 8 K, 2 BBMarcelo Mayer went 2-for-2 with a single, double, and two runs scored.Roman Anthony went 3-for-4 with three singles and a walk.Boston racked up 12 hits in its 3-0 win. Garrett Crochet pitched a gem as the Boston Red Sox edged out the Cincinnati Reds in their Opening Day matchup, 3-0. Crochet allowed only three hits and walked two while striking out eight over six scoreless innings. Boston's bullpen took care of business the rest of the way, with Justin Slaten, Garrett Whitlock, and Aroldis Chapman keeping Cincinnati scoreless. Ceddanne Rafaela, Trevor Story, and Jarren Duran knocked in the Red Sox' three runs. Marcelo Mayer didn't get the start, but he entered as a pinch-hitter and went 2-for-2 with two runs scored on the day. Roman Anthony went 3-for-4 with a walk. Check out our live blog below for a full Opening Day recap: The Boston Red Sox started their 2026 season with a 3-0 win over the Reds in Cincinnati. Garrett Crochet looked ready for another run at the American League Cy Young award. The Red Sox ace cruised through six scoreless innings, striking out eight Reds hitters and allowing only three hits while walking two. Boston's bullpen kept Cincinnati off the board for the final three innings. Justin Slaten and Garrett Whitlock bridged the gap to Aroldis Chapman, who slammed the door shut in the ninth. Offensively, the Red Sox tallied 12 hits. Roman Anthony went 3-for-4 with three singles and a walk, and fellow former top prospect Marcelo Mayer went 2-for-2 with a single and a double. Mayer wasn't in the starting lineup, but he doubled as a pinch-hitter for Isiah Kiner-Falefa in the seventh and scored the game's first run on a Ceddanne Rafaela single. The Red Sox hope to win games by preventing runs with an elite rotation and a solid infield defense. After his lights-out performance, Garrett Crochet spoke on how run prevention will be part of the team's identity in 2026: "We came into camp with the guys that we acquired knowing that we were gonna be in a good position to perform like that and to be able to answer those challenges, whether it be ground-ball defense in the infield or whatnot. The guys that we returned as well, all the confidence in the world. ... "It just felt like all day the ball was finding somebody. On days like that, you feel very good throwing strikes." Crochet on the team's identity as a run-preventing team 🔒 "All the confidence in the world... it just felt like all day the ball was finding somebody. On days like that, you feel very good throwing strikes."🎙️ presented by @WBMasonCo pic.twitter.com/xpfxE5sz45— NESN (@NESN) March 26, 2026 Red Sox relief pitcher Payton Tolle spoke to the media today about starting the season in AAA in Worcester, and what his mindset is to try and get called up to the Red Sox. The Boston Red Sox passed their first test of the 2026 season as they shut out the Cincinnati Reds on Opening Day, 3-0. Other than being kept off the scoreboard for the first six innings, the Red Sox looked sharp in every facet of the game. Garrett Crochet pitched a gem, the offense racked up 12 hits, and the bullpen kept Cincinnati scoreless for the final three innings. As always, Opening Day left us with plenty to overreact to with 161 games left in the regular season. Here are five instant overreactions to Boston's victory: The 2025 AL Cy Young runner-up looks poised for another run at the award this season. After a rough spring training, Crochet was in peak form in Cincinnati. Read Full Article Marcelo Mayer came through with a pinch-hit double in the seventh and scored the Red Sox' first run of the day on a Ceddanne Rafaela RBI single. After the win, Mayer was asked if he had experience as a pinch-hitter. "Zero," Mayer said with a smile. "You guys know that, they don't do that in the minors, but I did a little bit last year. Obviously, didn't do it this spring, but knew that was going to be a part of my role coming into this team, so just mentally preparing for that and making sure I'm ready to go for whenever that is." According to Alex Speier of The Boston Globe, Roman Anthony is the 14th 21-year-old ever to reach base four times on Opening Day. Nine of the first 13 are in the Hall of Fame. Roman Anthony went 3-for-4 with a walk in the Red Sox' win. Boston tallied 12 hits on the day. After the victory, Anthony spoke to NESN's Jahmai Webster about the offense's potential. "We got a tough group. We know what we're made of," Anthony said. "We've got a gritty lineup. We're in there, we're trying to scratch and claw any way we can." Score: 3-0 Red Sox, middle of the ninth inning The Red Sox will give Aroldis Chapman a comfortable lead to work with in the ninth. Jarren Duran hit an RBI single to right field, scoring Roman Anthony to make it 3-0. Score: 2-0 Red Sox, top of the ninth inning Marcelo Mayer led off the inning with a single off Reds reliever Connor Phillips, making him 2-for-2 on the day. Phillips struck out Carlos Narvaez and got Ceddanne Rafaela to fly out to left, but Roman Anthony kept the inning alive with a two-out walk. Trevor Story knocked a single into left field, scoring Mayer from third for Boston's second run of the day. Score: 1-0 Red Sox, end of the eighth inning Garrett Whitlock entered the game for the Red Sox in the eighth, replacing Justin Slaten. Whitlock got Matt McLain to fly out, then struck out Elly De La Cruz before Sal Stewart hit one over the right-field wall for a ground-rule double, but Whitlock slammed the door shut on the eighth by striking out Eugenio Suarez to get his revenge for the World Baseball Classic. Suarez scored the go-ahead run for Venezuela off Whitlock in the WBC championship. Score: 1-0 Red Sox, middle of the eighth inning The Reds replaced reliever Sam Moll with Graham Ashcraft after Moll got Jarren Duran to ground out to shortstop. Ashcraft struck out Willson Contreras, then walked Caleb Durbin before getting Wilyer Abreu to ground out to end the inning. Score: 1-0 Red Sox, end of the seventh inning Red Sox reliever Justin Slaten walked the leadoff man Tyler Stephenson, but he bounced back by striking out Will Benson, getting Ke'Bryan Hayes to fly out to left, and striking out TJ Friedl. Score: 1-0 Red Sox, bottom of the seventh inning Red Sox reliever Justin Slaten is on the mound to replace Garrett Crochet. Crochet finishes with only three hits allowed, two walks, and eight strikeouts through six scoreless innings. Score: 1-0 Red Sox, middle of the seventh inning After Ceddanne Rafaela put the Red Sox' first run on the board, Roman Anthony struck out to make him 3-for-4 on the day. Trevor Story grounded out to second to end the inning. Score: 1-0 Red Sox, top of the seventh inning At last, a run has crossed the plate in Cincinnati. Marcelo Mayer pinch-hit for Isiah Kiner-Falefa with right-hander Pierce Johnson replacing Reds left-hander Andrew Abbott. Mayer doubled to center field for his first hit in his first at-bat of the season. After Carlos Narvaez bunted Mayer over to third base, Ceddanne Rafaela laced a single up the middle to get Mayer home. Score: 0-0, end of the sixth inning Garrett Crochet had his first scare of the day, but the ace got out of a bases-loaded jam to keep the game scoreless heading into the seventh. After getting TJ Friedl to ground out to shortstop, Crochet walked Matt McLain for his second BB of the day. Elly De La Cruz followed with a bloop single, and Sal Stewart loaded the bases with a line drive to right. Crochet locked in, striking out Eugenio Suarez and Spencer Steer for his seventh and eighth Ks of the day to escape the jam. Score: 0-0, middle of the sixth inning Reds starter Andrew Abbott got through a 1-2-3 inning with a Willson Contreras pop out (Elly De La Cruz laid out to make the grab), Caleb Durbin groundout, and a Wilyer Abreu strikeout. Score: 0-0, end of the fifth inning Garrett Crochet is through five scoreless innings in Cincinnati. The Red Sox ace started the inning off by striking out Spencer Steer. After Tyler Stephenson reached on an error by Red Sox third baseman Caleb Durbin, Crochet K'd Noelvi Marte for his sixth of the day. Ke'Bryan Hayes flew out to left to end the inning. Crochet has six strikeouts. Score: 0-0, middle of the fifth inning The Red Sox still can't get runs on the board despite having seven hits through five innings. After Carlos Narvaez fouled out to first, Ceddanne Rafaela hit an infield single. Roman Anthony then smoked one 110.2 mph off Reds first baseman Sal Stewart, who was hurt on the play but stayed in the game. Anthony is 3-for-3 on the day. With runners on first and second, Reds starter Andrew Abbott got out of the jam by striking out Trevor Story and Jarren Duran to end the inning. Score: 0-0, end of the fourth inning Another 1-2-3 inning for Garrett Crochet. The Red Sox ace struck out Elly De La Cruz to start the inning, got Sal Stewart to ground out to third on a nice play by Caleb Durbin, then struck out Eugenio Suarez looking on the Red Sox' first ABS challenge of the season. Crochet has four strikeouts on the day. Score: 0-0, middle of the fourth inning Reds lefty Andrew Abbott got through the fourth with only eight pitches. He got Caleb Durbin to fly out to right, Wilyer Abreu to ground out to short, and Isiah Kiner-Falefa to ground out to third. Score: 0-0, end of the third inning Garrett Crochet is up to only 33 pitches through three after another 1-2-3 inning. He got Ke'Bryan Hayes and TJ Friedl to line out before K'ing Matt McLain for his second strikeout of the day. Score: 0-0, middle of the third inning Roman Anthony led off the top of the third with a single to left field for his second hit of the day. The Red Sox were again unable to capitalize, however, as Trevor Story flew out to left, Jarren Duran popped up to the shortstop, and Willson Contreras grounded out to end the inning. Score: 0-0, end of the second inning After a 1-2-3 first inning, the Reds earned their first hit of the day off Garrett Crochet with a double by top prospect Sal Stewart to lead off the second. After offseason addition Eugenio Suarez flew out to right field, Spencer Steer walked on four pitches to put runners on first and second. Tyler Stephenson flew out to deep left field for the second out, then Crochet struck out Noelvi Marte to end the inning. Score: 0-0, middle of the second inning Wilyer Abreu led off the second inning with an infield single. After an Isiah Kiner-Falefa strikeout, Carlos Narvaez slapped a line-drive single into right field to put runners on first and second. Ceddanne Rafaela grounded into an inning-ending double play for Boston's second double play of the day. The Red Sox have four hits off Reds starter Andrew Abbott, but nothing to show for it. Score: 0-0, end of the first inning Red Sox ace Garrett Crochet made quick work of the top of the Reds lineup in the first inning. It took him only four pitches as TJ Friedl grounded out, Matt McLain flew out, and Elly De La Cruz grounded out. Score: 0-0, middle of the first inning Red Sox star Roman Anthony singled up the middle on the first pitch of the game by Reds left-hander Andrew Abbott. Unfortunately for Boston, the next batter Trevor Story grounded into a double play. With two outs, Jarren Duran reached on an infield single and later stole second base. Willson Contreras walked to put runners on first and second, but Caleb Durbin grounded out for out No. 3. Red Sox top pitching prospect Payton Tolle didn't make the Opening Day roster, but he's laser-focused on getting back to the big leagues. "Something that's been stuck in my head is, 'get back,'" Tolle said in Worcester. Red Sox relief pitcher Payton Tolle spoke to the media today about starting the season in AAA in Worcester, and what his mindset is to try and get called up to the Red Sox. The Red Sox have an outfield/designated hitter logjam with Roman Anthony, Ceddanne Rafaela, Wilyer Abreu, Jarren Duran, and Masataka Yoshida on the depth chart. Manager Alex Cora addressed the issue before Opening Day, per Ian Browne of MLB.com. "We'll see how it plays out. I don't want Roman to become a DH. I don't want JD (Jarren Duran) to become a DH," Cora said. "Like I said before, when Ceddanne doesn't play center field, JD will play center field. When Wilyer doesn't play right field, JD will play left field. Roman will play right. And then we have to mix in Masa. So I know it's going to be a topic throughout 162 plus and I respect that. But there's nothing behind it, analytic-wise, information-wise, they're really good at what they do, all of them. "So, taking care of them physically is very important. Throughout the seasons, Wily hasn't been able to post every day. JD has been able to do that. Ceddanne towards the end of season has tailed off so having five is going to help us make sure everybody's fresh when it matters." Check out our eight-part Red Sox season preview series below: Read Full ArticleCould Roman Anthony ever be the biggest star in Boston? Michael Holley and Andrew Callahan discuss his superstar status after huge performance at WBC Opinions about the 2026 Boston Red Sox are mixed heading into Thursday's season opener in Cincinnati. Some are optimistic about the club after it took a step forward in 2025 and ended its four-year postseason drought. Others are hesitant to buy in because of the front office's reluctance to spend on big-name free agents during the offseason. Wherever you stand on this year's group, there are plenty of reasons to be invested in the 2026 campaign. Roman Anthony is ready to prove he's one of the league's biggest stars, Garrett Crochet is eyeing the Cy Young award after finishing as the runner-up, and the rest of the rotation is expected to form one of the best units in the entire league. After standout performances in the World Baseball Classic, Wilyer Abreu and Jarren Duran are candidates for All-Star seasons. Willson Contreras and Caleb Durbin are intriguing additions to the lineup, and Marcelo Mayer hopes to carve out a consistent role with the club after a mixed bag of a rookie year. Read Full ArticleHolley, Giles and Keefe discuss Sam Kennedy’s recent comments about his expectations for the team and John Henry resurfacing on X The American League East will be arguably MLB's toughest division in 2026. At least four of the five clubs will have a legitimate shot to win the division. Even the consensus last-place club, the Tampa Bay Rays, is talented enough to finish the campaign with a winning record. The Red Sox went 89-75 last year to place third in the AL East and earn a Wild Card spot. They finished behind the Toronto Blue Jays and New York Yankees, who had the same record at 94-68. All three clubs are expected to be among the AL's best this upcoming season, and the Baltimore Orioles spent big over the winter in hopes of joining them. This is undoubtedly the most difficult division to predict, but that's what we'll attempt to do ahead of MLB's Opening Night on Wednesday. Read Full Article
